This document presents a visualization of historical daily average temperatures in Boston, Massachusetts, from 1940 to 2026. The data is retrieved from the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API.

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)

# 1. Load the temperature data
temp_data <- read_csv("boston_temperatures.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Map all historical dates to a single dummy year (2020, a leap year) 
# to stack the temperatures by day of the year.
temp_data <- temp_data %>%
  mutate(
    dummy_date = as.Date(paste0("2020-", format(date, "%m-%d")))
  )

# 3. Identify the last 3 days of the dataset (June 19, 20, and 21, 2026)
last_3_days <- temp_data %>%
  arrange(desc(date)) %>%
  slice(1:3)

# 4. Configure custom labels for months on the x-axis
month_breaks <- as.Date(paste0("2020-", 1:12, "-01"))
month_labels <- c("Jan.", "Feb.", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "Aug.", "Sept.", "Oct.", "Nov.", "Dec.")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7.8
#| fig-align: center
#| label: plot

# 5. Build the plot replicating the clean style of the Portland chart
ggplot() +
  # Draw historical background dots (dense light grey points)
  geom_point(
    data = temp_data,
    aes(x = dummy_date, y = temp_mean_f),
    color = "#7f8c8d",
    alpha = 0.18,
    size = 0.6
  ) +
  # Draw highlight dots for the last 3 days (warm red)
  geom_point(
    data = last_3_days,
    aes(x = dummy_date, y = temp_mean_f),
    color = "#b33d26",
    size = 3.0
  ) +
  # Add the bold red label next to the highlighted points
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = as.Date("2020-06-25"),
    y = mean(last_3_days$temp_mean_f),
    label = "Last 3 days",
    color = "#b33d26",
    fontface = "bold",
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = 0.5,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  # Configure axis scales
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = month_breaks,
    labels = month_labels,
    expand = c(0.01, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  # Adjust y limits using coord_cartesian to avoid filtering out cold winter values (< 0°F)
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(-15, 105)
  ) +
  # Titles & axis unit label placement
  labs(
    title = "Daily average temperatures in Boston, 1940-2026",
    subtitle = "100 deg. Fahrenheit"
  ) +
  # Minimalist styling theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e0e0e0", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    # Title & Subtitle fonts
    plot.title = element_text(family = "sans", face = "bold", size = 18, color = "black", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "serif", size = 11, color = "#222222", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    # Axis typography & lines
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(family = "serif", size = 11, color = "#222222"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(family = "serif", size = 11, color = "#222222", margin = margin(t = 5)),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(5, "pt"),
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5)
  )
```
